id.description: Identifier of the Elementor document to read. Call elementor-document-list for the documents Elementor controls.

type.description: The WordPress post type: page, post, or elementor_library for a saved template.

status.description: The WordPress post status, such as publish or draft.

editMode.description: The stored Elementor edit mode, normally builder. Empty when the stored value is unreadable.

nodes.description: The document's top-level elements, each carrying its own children, in stored order.

nodeCount.description: How many elements the whole tree holds, at every level.

maxDepth.description: How many nesting LEVELS the tree has, not the greatest depth value: a tree whose deepest element sits at depth 2 reports 3, and an empty tree reports 0.

widgetTypeCounts.description: How many times each widget type appears, keyed by widget type. Empty when the tree holds no widgets.

pageSettings.description: This page's Elementor page settings. Enough to reproduce the page elsewhere: the layout it actually renders with, whether the theme title is hidden, and the whole stored row behind both.

layoutSync.description: Elementor keeps a page's layout in two rows: the one its editor panel reads, and the page template WordPress renders from. They normally agree. When they do not, the page renders with the second one and the Elementor editor shows the first, which is reported here rather than guessed at.

inEffect.description: The layout the page is actually rendered with.

pageSettingsLayout.description: The layout Elementor's own page-settings row claims, which is what its editor panel shows.

agree.description: False when the two rows disagree. Setting the layout again with elementor-page-settings-set writes both and brings them back into step.

storedSettings.description: The page settings exactly as the row stores them, under Elementor's own key names, including the background, padding and responsive values nothing here writes. A page whose settings have never been touched stores no row and answers an empty object.

layout.description: Which page layout this page is actually rendered with, read from the page template WordPress serves it from. A page whose template is the theme's own, or one Elementor no longer offers, reports the default.

hideTitle.description: Whether the theme's page title is hidden on this page.

hints.description: Authoring warnings this particular page has earned, each detected from what is actually stored rather than offered as general advice. Always present, and an empty list when this page has nothing to warn about.

message.description: What the condition means for this page and which operation changes it.

id.description: Elementor's own element identifier, carried through unchanged, so it is stable across reads whenever it is present. Null means the stored element declares no identifier — such an element cannot be addressed by a write, and null is never unique within a document.

elType.description: The stored element type, such as container or widget. Empty when the stored element declares none.

widgetType.description: The stored widget type for a widget element, and null for anything else.

kind.description: Either widget or container, derived from elType. An element declaring no type is reported as a container.

label.description: A short human string naming what this element is. DERIVED on every read from elType and widgetType, stored nowhere, and for display only — never record it as a stored value.

depth.description: This element's zero-based nesting depth, so a top-level element is 0.

childCount.description: How many children this element has, counting only the ones this response returns.

children.description: This element's children, in stored order.
